Article.ArticleTitle: Lysosomal proteomics reveals mechanisms of neuronal APOE4-associated lysosomal dysfunction.

Abstract.AbstractText: APOE4 is the primary risk factor for Alzheimer disease (AD). Early AD pathological events first affect the neuronal endolysosomal system, which in turn causes neuronal protein aggregation and cell death. Despite the crucial influence of lysosomes upon AD pathophysiology, and that APOE4 localizes to lysosomes, the influence of APOE4 on lysosomal function remains unexplored. We find that expression of APOE4 in neuronal cell lines results in lysosomal alkalinization and impaired lysosomal function. To identify driving factors for these defects, we performed quantitative lysosomal proteome profiling. This revealed that APOE4 expression results in differential regulation of numerous lysosomal proteins, correlating with APOE allele status and disease severity in AD brains. In particular, APOE4 expression results in the depletion of lysosomal LGALS3BP and the accumulation of lysosomal TMED5. We additionally validated that these lysosomal protein changes can be targeted to modulate lysosomal function. Nevan J. Krogan has previously held financially compensated consulting agreements with the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai, New York, and Twist Bioscience Corp. Swaney has financially compensated consulting agreements with Maze Therapeutics and Rezo Therapeutics. The authors have no additional financial interests.
